description: A stereo looper that records a second of audio, plays it back over and over, and lets you speed it up and blend it against the incoming signal

params.text: Sets how much of the buffer is played back before it wraps, 15% to 90% of one second
Multiplies the left input on the way in and the recorded loop on the way out, 0 to 2
Blends between the incoming signal and the loop, 0 to 1, starting at half of each
Starts recording a new loop from the two inputs, wiping what was there
Wipes the loop back to silence
Multiplies the playback speed: +0 plays at speed, +1 doubles it for an octave up, +2 trebles it and +3 quadruples it for two octaves up

inputs.text: The left channel of the audio to be recorded and mixed against the loop
The right channel of the audio to be recorded and mixed against the loop
A rising edge starts recording a new loop, as the SAMPLE button does
A rising edge wipes the loop, as the DELETE button does
Added to the LENGTH knob at a tenth of the buffer per volt
Added to the DRY/WET knob at a tenth per volt
A voltage above 1V steps the playback speed up by one more multiple than the OCT+ switch alone gives

outputs.text: Carries the left channel, the loop blended against the incoming signal and clamped to ±5V
Carries the right channel, the loop blended against the incoming signal and clamped to ±5V

notes: the module does nothing until a loop has been recorded; press SAMPLE or send a pulse to the SAMPLE jack with audio at the inputs
recording begins at the first moment the left input reads exactly 0V, so a loop started against silence will not begin until signal arrives
the buffer is one second of audio at a 48kHz sample rate, and the LENGTH control chooses how much of it plays
the recorded audio is written into the patch file sample by sample, so a patch holding this module is very large and slow to save
the GAIN knob is applied to the left input and to a right channel taken from the left, but not to a right input with its own cable
the OCT+ switch reads +0 to +3 but sets a playback rate of one to four times, so only +1 and +3 are whole octaves

continuous · one channel only

inputs.3: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0.1 to 1V.
